# SlimToken

> SlimToken is a Rust engine that plans an objective into a task DAG and runs
> the DAG as one parallel wave of model calls. An adaptive controller sets
> the in-flight width. A repair wave fixes failed tasks with the error as
> context. The engine is provider-neutral: every model call goes through one
> `ModelClient` trait. A host harness owns model wiring, gates, and judgment.

Measured on Muse and DeepSeek, 2026-10 to 2026-11:

- A 20-file app, plan to files: about 13 s wall on DeepSeek.
- Aggregate output rate, one wave: about 1,500 to 1,800 tok/s. One stream
  alone gives about 130 to 150 tok/s.
- Concurrency knee (Muse): 1,147 tok/s at 32 streams. Knee at 24 to 32.
- Largest-first admission: minus 25.7% wave time on Muse.
- Patience-bounded repair injection: minus 31% retry volume.

## Install

- Engine: `cargo build --release` in this repo. The binary is
  `target/release/slimtoken` (or `slimtoken.exe` on Windows).
- QA sidecar: `npm install --global sidecars/qa`, then
  `slimtoken-qa validate --strict build/`.
- Library: `slimtoken = { path = "." }` in a Rust host, or the crates.io
  package when it publishes.

## Run from the CLI

```
slimtoken run --architect --objective "Build a Python CLI that ..." \
  --provider deepseek --output slimtoken-out \
  --test-cmd "python -I check-build.py <deps-dir>"
```

Providers are presets. A preset fills the base URL, model, worker effort,
planner effort, planner schema, and the key env var.

| Preset | Base URL | Model | Key env var |
|---|---|---|---|
| `muse` | `https://api.meta.ai/v1` | muse-spark-1.3-contributor | `MUSE_API_KEY` |
| `deepseek` | `https://api.deepseek.com/v1` | deepseek-flash | `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` |
| `anthropic` | `https://api.anthropic.com/v1` | claude-sonnet-5-5 | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |

The `anthropic` preset pins conservative starting points, not measurements:
effort `low`, planner schema off, burst cap 8. Any other OpenAI-compatible
server works with `--base-url URL --model NAME`; SlimToken appends
`/chat/completions` to the base URL. Put the key in `--api-key` or in
`OPENAI_API_KEY`. Never put a key in a file that git tracks.

The engine and the harness can use different models. A harness can run its
own management model and hand all worker tasks to SlimToken with a cheap
fast model. Each model is a separate `--provider` (or a separate
`slimtoken serve` instance). A run never switches models mid-run.

## Embed in a harness

Two seams. Pick one.

1. **REST, no Rust**: `slimtoken serve --port 8080` (build with
   `--features serve`). The host POSTs a run to `/v1/runs`, polls
   `/v1/runs/{id}`, and reads `/v1/runs/{id}/report`. One serve instance
   serves one model; run several instances to split models. Full contract:
   [API.md](API.md).
2. **Rust library**: implement `ModelClient` (or wrap the shipped
   OpenAI-compatible client) and pass `Arc<dyn ModelClient>` to
   `RunManager::new`. The engine owns planning, waves, cache priming, and
   repair; the host owns the model, the optional stack profile, the
   assembled deliverable, and the gate command. Reference loop:
   [examples/host-harness.rs](examples/host-harness.rs). Full guide:
   [EMBEDDING.md](EMBEDDING.md).

## Capabilities as sidecar packs

Sidecar packs bolt onto the engine or onto build output. They are separate
npm packages under `sidecars/`. They never enter the engine core. Packs
ship a gate command, a report, and a JSON twin; most spend zero model
tokens. Catalog and extension contract: [sidecars/README.md](sidecars/README.md).

## Evidence rule

No performance claim ships without a paired A/B run on the same workload.
Numbers above are such pairs, one arm off and one arm on, interleaved.
